MGT 409 · AI Foundations for Managers · Final project

ED Cost Estimator

"How much am I going to get charged?" An answer in 16 seconds, from the hospital's own published prices.

Reema Panjwani

The problem

Nobody can tell an ED patient what the visit will cost

155.4MED visits in the U.S. in 2022 (CDC)
5×spread for one service: a level 4 visit is $321 to $1,712 across 23 insurers at Yale New Haven
724,913rows in the hospital's public price file, organized by billing code
28%of adults skipped or delayed care over cost in the past year (KFF, 2026)
  • The price is set after care: a visit level, plus every test that was ordered.
  • The legal right to a "good faith estimate" does not cover walk-in or same-day care.
  • So patients decide blind, and the bill arrives weeks later.
What is new

Start from symptoms, not billing codes

What exists today

  • Hospital and insurer estimators: you must already know which service you need.
  • FAIR Health, Turquoise: built around a procedure, or area averages.
  • Goodbill: only after the bill arrives.
  • A general AI model: asked the same price twice, it said $60, then $107. The hospital's file says $119.

This app

  • You describe the problem in a sentence.
  • It predicts the likely ED workup.
  • It prices each line at this hospital's rate for your insurer.
  • It gives a low, likely and high figure, and says why.
  • It covers "what if I'm admitted?"
  • The AI cannot invent a number.
How it works

Four agents in a fixed line; code does the math

GreenAI agents, all on gpt-6-luna Sandplain code, zero tokens. The cheapest agent goes first and can end the run.

Demo · a real run

"My dad is 58 and has had chest pressure for 30 minutes"

  • First: go now. The warning appears before any AI call.
  • Then: about $1,764 under his Aetna plan, from $1,392 to $2,015.
  • If admitted: his share stops at the $5,000 out-of-pocket maximum.

Each agent's tool calls and tokens. Here: the planner finds the chest pain scenario; the analyst matches Aetna and prices it.

Did cutting cost hurt?

Not on what was measured: both settings picked the same scenario, codes, insurer and totals. The wording of summaries was not scored. Five cases is a small sample.

Safety

The biggest risk: a price that talks someone out of care

  • Care first. Warning signs trigger "call 911 or go now" in code. An agent can add a flag, never remove one.
  • Attacks. Injection is refused before any tokens are spent. No agent can read files or keys.
  • Made-up facts. Unknown billing codes are rejected. Every dollar must match the pricing code.
  • Runaway spend. Caps per run, per minute and per day.

Impact

From "nobody knows" to a number in 16 seconds

15.6 sto an itemized, insurer-specific estimate (my tests, five cases)
6–14billing codes a patient would otherwise have to find among 724,913 rows
$2,271 → $1,340list price vs cash price for a cut finger: the app tells uninsured patients to ask
  • Patients: a figure to plan around, and the right questions.
  • Hospital: could ease the load on billing staff. Not measured yet.
  • New: the "if you're admitted" conversation rarely happens in the ED today.

Limits and what's next

Honest about what it does not do yet

Limits today

  • Hospital bill only. The physician bills separately.
  • One hospital.
  • No traditional Medicare or Medicaid rates in the hospital's file.
  • 17 scenario templates, reviewed by one clinician, not yet checked against real bills.

With another month

  • Add the physician's bill.
  • Validate against published real ED bills.
  • "Check my bill" when it arrives.
  • More hospitals: they all publish the same file format.
  • Pilot with a hospital's financial counselors.
